brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Base pieces at level 0 (piece 0,0,0 full; 1,0,0 half-e; 0,-1,0 full) and level 1 (piece 0,0,1 full; 0,-1,1 full), joined by snaps.
bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) and bin:0,-1,1~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments) sit in the two level-1 cells.
Notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) at 1,-1,level 0, between the level-0 bases, under the open level-1 cell. It was the only drawer position the configurator offered.
capOpenFaces added 16 solid caps on every open face; lockJoints added a joint bolt. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex workbench organizer: a level-0 base row carrying a notch drawer, and two level-1 bases carrying two divided bins. All open faces are capped and the joints are locked. check_build is clean (meshClash clear). The build has 46 parts, a little over the ~40 guideline, because the caps and snaps add parts. No props were added since the brief did not ask for them. I did not verify the drawer's pull-out motion or the bins' contents beyond the configurator's fit checks, and material choice (strength, water, etc.) is outside what the configurator checks.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
